correctness.rationale: Every exponent class modulo six is covered. Integral interpolation by \(64^t\) and \(729^t\) gives the first normalized interpolation equal to \(2+6t\) and the second to \(2+6t^2\). Bounds \(j-1-\nu_7(j!)\ge1\) for \(j\ge2\) and \(j-2-\nu_7(j!)\ge1\) for \(j\ge3\) justify discarded coefficients. Explicit zero lifts \(-1/3\), \(-1/2\), \(-2/3\) and simple-root differences yield precise valuations, and CRT yields counts 2,8,15 for all levels. The Python verifier passed 5000 exact modular cases, five complete period levels, ten special indices; these computations supplement proof.
